_doc: Record layouts for the binary map assets under src/data/maps/.
This file is the schema, and it is the point of the whole arrangement: the .bin
files are the source of truth for the BYTES, and this file is the source of truth
for what those bytes MEAN. tools/render_map_asm.py reads both and emits the
annotated .asm that the ROM is actually assembled from.
So documenting a newly-understood field is an edit HERE, not a code change, and
not 21 hand edits: name the field once and every map's generated .asm improves.
The same schema is what a map editor should read, so the record layout is not
defined separately in Python, in JS and in an asm comment.
JSON rather than TOML only because tomllib needs Python 3.11 and the rest of the
build runs on 3.10. Comments therefore live in _doc / doc keys.

ENTITY_ID.doc: Entity type ids, scraped from the contiguous run of DEF lines between the two symbols below. Scoped by span rather than by an ENTITY_* prefix match on purpose: constants.asm reuses that prefix for ENTITY_FIELD_*, ENTITY_SLOT_*, ENTITY_SPAWN_*_OFFSET and friends, which are unrelated enums that would otherwise collide on value.

MAP_ID.doc: Map / level ids. Same span trick as above: constants.asm also uses MAP_ for the scroll-direction bits and the tile-animation modes, which are unrelated enums.

doc: One record per placed object, walked by call_0a_4000_EntityList_LoadForCurrentLevel
in bank0A_entity_load.asm. Field offsets below are exactly the
ENTITY_SPAWN_*_OFFSET constants in src/constants/constants.asm - if you retune
one there, change it here too.
Record order is load-bearing: wD000_EntityFlags is indexed by an entry's
position in the list, so inserting a record renumbers every flag after it.
That is why each record's index is emitted as a comment.
NOTE: offsets +7/+8 are named the other way round here than in constants.asm.
In all 857 records byte +7 >= byte +8, exactly as +5 >= +6 for the X axis, so
both axes store max then min and ENTITY_SPAWN_BOUNDINGBOX_YMIN_OFFSET /
_YMAX_OFFSET look swapped. Renaming those two constants is cosmetic and would
leave `make check` passing.

lines.comment: room bounds in blocks, each axis max then min
free parameters, meaning is per entity type
spare - not read by any code found so far

doc: One level's doors, searched by call_0b_4efe_Map_SetSpawnPosition in
bank0B_map_spawns.asm. The search is linear and takes the first match, but no
list holds two records with the same source block, so record order never
matters here - unlike the entity lists.
Everything is in BLOCK coordinates: the grid the blockmap is laid out in, 128 x
128 blocks per level. One block is SPAWN_UNITS_PER_BLOCK ($20) units of player
world position, so the routine shifts these up by 5 and adds a per-case offset.
A record is one-directional. Most come in pairs, a record and its exact reverse,
which is what makes a door walkable both ways; the rest drop the player
somewhere they cannot walk back from. Thursday the 12th is the extreme case,
which is how a level whose mission is "find the items in the time given" is
built as a maze out of nothing but door records.

lines.comment: from block x, from block y, to block x, to block y

doc: Where the player lands when they step back out of a TV into the Media Dimension,
in blocks. Indexed by wD628_MediaDimensionRespawnPoint, which bank02 computes as
(TV entity list index - 1) / 2 when a TV is entered - and that works out to a
LEVEL ID. So each level effectively records where its own TV stands in the hub,
and the player is put back in front of whichever TV they came out of.
The empty entries are exactly the ten MAP_UNUSED_* slots, which is corroboration
that the index really is a map id.
CHECKPOINTS_PER_LEVEL block coordinate pairs per level, indexed by
levelId * 8 + wD618_CheckpointSpawnId * 2. Checkpoint 0 is where the level
starts; the rest are set by call_00_208c_Checkpoint_WriteSpawnId when the player
smashes a checkpoint TV block.
Only 20 of the 31 levels define a start at all, only 7 of those define a
checkpoint 1, and NO level uses checkpoint 2 or 3 - so the whole upper half of
every record is dead weight, and 194 of the 248 bytes here are zero.

lines.comment: checkpoints 0-3, each a block x, block y pair

block.doc: World position -> block coordinate. One block is $20 world units (SPAWN_UNITS_PER_BLOCK); the blockmap is 128x128 blocks.
